title: Yanliao Biota
summary: The Yanliao Biota is a Jurassic fossil assemblage of northern China, also called the Daohugou Biota, with exceptionally preserved insects, vertebrates and plants. High-precision dating of the Jianchang section places it near 160 million years ago, and it holds the oldest documented feathered dinosaurs. It declined around 155 Ma as the climate dried.

uncertainty.note: Jianchang ash beds date to 160.889-160.254 Ma; the Daohugou beds are described as Middle Jurassic to earliest Late Jurassic; decline ca. 155 Ma. The id's -165my is only a lookup key.

where.modern_name: Daohugou Village, Ningcheng County, Inner Mongolia, China
where.historical_name: Not applicable (Jurassic; no polity); fossil locality at Daohugou

importance.justification: Source of the oldest documented feathered dinosaurs and a diverse Jurassic insect fauna, preceding the Jehol Biota.

sources.title: High-precision age constraints on the Jurassic rise of feathered dinosaurs and eutherian mammals: U-Pb geochronology of the Yanliao Biota from Jianchang
sources.author: Chu, Ramezani, He, Bowring
